title: A novel Dy4III cluster constructed by a multidentate 8-hydroxyquinoline Schiff base ligand: Structure and slow magnetic relaxation behavior

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: [Dy4(TTA)4L4(H2O)2]·4CH3OH; H2L = 2-[(4-methyl-6-carboxyphenyl)imino]methyl-8-hydroxyquinoline (SI; main text inconsistently names a 4-methoxyphenyl analogue), TTA = 2-thenoyltrifluoroacetone

material_class.structural_family: tetranuclear Dy4 parallelogram bridged by phenolate μ-O and carboxylate oxygen atoms of L2-

synthesis.procedure: H2L was prepared by aldimine condensation of 2-amino-5-methylbenzoic acid (12.0 mmol) with 8-hydroxyquinoline-2-carboxaldehyde (12.0 mmol) in ethanol, stirred at room temperature for 6 h; the yellow precipitate was washed with ethanol, dried in vacuo, and purified by column chromatography (1/3 dichloromethane/petroleum ether containing 1% triethylamine) to give a deep yellow solid (2.51 g, 68.1%). Dy(TTA)3·2H2O was prepared by a literature method. Cluster 1: a solution of Dy(TTA)3·2H2O (0.025 mmol, 0.0215 g) in 15 mL n-heptane was refluxed for 3 h, cooled to 75 °C, and treated with H2L (0.025 mmol, 0.0077 g) in CH2Cl2 (3 mL). The mixture was stirred for 1 h at 75 °C, cooled to room temperature, filtered, kept in the dark, and concentrated by slow evaporation at 4 °C. Needle-shaped red crystals formed after 3 days.
synthesis.temperature: ligand: room temperature; cluster: reflux, then 75 °C, then room temperature; crystallization at 4 °C
synthesis.time: ligand: 6 h; cluster: 3 h reflux plus 1 h at 75 °C; crystals after 3 days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reflux followed by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration, storage in the dark, slow evaporation at 4 °C; needle-shaped red crystals after 3 days
synthesis.yield: cluster 1: 33% based on Dy; H2L: 2.51 g, 68.1%

properties.summary: Cluster 1 shows slow magnetic relaxation under zero dc field: χ″ is frequency dependent below 10 K with no peaks down to 2.0 K, ascribed to quantum tunneling of the magnetization. χMT falls from 56.64 cm^3 K mol^-1 at 300 K (near the 56.89 cm^3 K mol^-1 expected for four DyIII ions) to 38.15 cm^3 K mol^-1 at 2.0 K, attributed to weak antiferromagnetic exchange and/or thermal depopulation of DyIII Stark sublevels. Magnetization at 2.0 K does not saturate (23.05 Nβ at 80 kOe versus 40 Nβ theoretical), and M vs H/T curves (2.0–8.0 K) do not superimpose. An approximate barrier is ΔE/kB ≈ 1.47 K with τ0 ≈ 4.4×10^-6 s. Luminescence instrumentation is mentioned, but no optical data are reported.

measurements.conditions: 300 K, dc field 1.0 kOe (1000 Oe), solid state, MPMS-XL7
